description: Temporary, expiring acceptance for the reviewed node-forge Expo developer-tooling advisory. The source-map-js exception was removed after patching; the braces exception was removed because the advisory is no longer present in the registry audit. No expiry is extended, and every other live advisory remains a failure.

exceptions.title: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements
exceptions.reachability: Developer-machine CLI tooling only, not device-reachable application code. The originally reviewed paths were expo 57.0.28 -> @expo/cli 57.0.29 -> node-forge 1.4.0 and @expo/cli 57.0.29 -> @expo/code-signing-certificates 0.0.6 -> node-forge 1.4.0. The October 26 lockfile update changes Expo to 57.0.30 and its nested CLI to 57.0.31; node-forge 1.4.0, code-signing-certificates 0.0.6, the affected-package set, and the application configuration remain unchanged. This patch does not extend the October 30 acceptance. @expo/cli is the `expo` command binary (expo's package.json bin entry); expo's runtime entry does not import it, no app source imports node-forge, @expo/cli, or @expo/code-signing-certificates, and the deterministic iOS and Android exports contain no node-forge code. Inside the CLI, node-forge RSA verification runs in exactly two places, both in the development-server manifest signer: validateSelfSignedCertificate checks the self-signature of a project's own updates.codeSigningCertificate read from local disk, and signBufferRSASHA256AndVerify re-verifies a signature the CLI has just produced with its own private key. Neither path accepts an attacker-chosen signature as an authorization decision, and both are unreachable here because app.json sets neither updates.codeSigningCertificate nor extra.eas.projectId and expo-updates is not installed. The app's own approval signatures use @noble/curves P-256, not RSA.

no_upstream_fix.how_checked: GitHub advisory GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv lists no first patched version. The npm registry shows node-forge 1.4.0 (2026-03-24) as the latest release and dist-tag. Upstream has no tag after v1.4.0; the fix is the open, unmerged digitalbazaar/forge#1152. Every Expo CLI line checked still depends on node-forge ^1.3.3 and @expo/code-signing-certificates ^0.0.6: @expo/cli 57.0.26, 57.0.27 (latest), 58.1.1 (next), and the 58 canary. @expo/code-signing-certificates 0.0.7 (2026-09-30) only raises its node-forge floor to ^1.4.0, which is still inside the advisory range.
no_upstream_fix.why_suggested_fix_rejected: expo@44.0.6 is thirteen SDK majors behind, predates the bundled @expo/cli, and targets react-native 0.64.3 rather than the pinned 0.86.3; it would trade one unreachable tooling advisory for an unsupported runtime. Overriding node-forge to an unreleased upstream branch would pull unreviewed code into the mobile approval boundary and bypass the seven-day release quarantine.

exceptions.revisit_trigger: When node-forge publishes a release outside <=1.4.0 and it clears this app's seven-day min-release-age, refresh the lock so @expo/cli resolves it through its ^1.3.3 range, require a zero-advisory npm audit, and delete this entry. Revisit immediately if app.json gains updates.codeSigningCertificate or extra.eas.projectId, if expo-updates is added, if any app source imports node-forge or @expo/code-signing-certificates, if an exported bundle contains node-forge, or if severity or affected packages change.
